violations.text: Dishes and utensils were observed in the hand-washing sink. A hand-washing sink must not be used for purposes other than hand washing. Dishes were relocated. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/06/2026
The last shellfish was used from the bag must be noted on the shellfish tag. New Violation. Correct By: 08/06/2026

Food contact surfaces of equipment/utensils (ice machines) were observed with an accumulation bio-film. The food contact surfaces of equipment must be clean to sight and touch. Ice machines were turned off and ice disposed of. PIC purchased bagged ice at the time of inspection. Ice machine to be cleaned and sanitized before use. New Violation. Correct By: 08/06/2026

Various foods were observed held above 41 degrees Fahrenheit. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Food that was recently moved from the walk-in was moved back to walk-in. Food in units over night was disposed of. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/06/2026
Utensils were observed stored in stagnant water between uses. Proper storage procedures reviewed with PIC. Items relocated or hot held. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/06/2026

The lowboy in the corner of the cookline and lowboy in the pizza prep area were observed in poor repair. Food on the top shelf of the cookline unit were observed at an elevated temperature (47-48 Degrees). Per PIC, food was moved from walk-in less than 2 hours ago. Food in the pizza prep unit was observed at 46-47 degrees. Food in unit was left over night. Disposed of. Service call to be placed. Units to not be used for TCS foods until units are serviced. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/06/2026
The facility is lacking thermo labels or similar internal temperature indicating device for the dish machine . New Violation. Correct By: 08/06/2026
The grout in the warewashing area was in poor repair. The floor in the ice machine was observed in poor repair. New Violation. Correct By: 11/30/2026

Proper cooling methods were not used for time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. Marinara was placed hot (86DF) in the walk-in in covered plastic containers greater than four inches deep. Per PIC marinara was pulled from stove top recently and was placed in an ice bath after. Marinara was removed from ice bath too soon. Any food cooling should reach 41 degrees or lower prior to covering. Food was moved back to ice bath to finish cooling process. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 10/03/2024
